name: QuickSwap Market
rootCause: Market.xyz had been utilizing the Curve LP Oracle for their lending and borrowing markets. However, a price manipulation vulnerability arose because of the presence of Read-Only Reentrancy in the Curve LP Oracle. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://polygonscan.com/tx/0xb8efe839da0c89daa763f39f30577dc21937ae351c6f99336a0017e63d387558 https://polygonscan.com/tx/0x303c770b81d8866693aa341774eaa2cd5dc3a5f1d2ad855b9d6f0c10b5c36d5d Analysis: The attack flow as follow: 1. Execute a flashloan of WMATIC and stMATIC tokens. 2. Provide liquidity to the WMATIC/stMATIC Curve pool and receive Curve LP tokens. 3. Utilize a portion of the Curve LP tokens as collateral on http://market.xyz. 4. Increase the collateral's value by removing liquidity from the Curve pool. 1. when removing the liquidity, D value remain unchanged but total supply already updated. 2. more: https://chainsecurity.com/curve-lp-oracle-manipulation-post-mortem/ 5. Use the expensive collateral to borrow MAI using a fallback function. 6. Initiate self-liquidation to acquire the collateral at a discounted price. 7. Repay the flashloan. https://quillaudits.medium.com/decoding-220k-read-only-reentrancy-exploit-quillaudits-30871d728ad5

descriptions.text: QuickSwap's Market.xyz lending pool on Polygon was exploited on 24 October 2022 via a flash loan and Curve LP oracle manipulation. The attacker distorted collateral prices to borrow more funds, resulting in losses around $220,000. The incident led QuickSwap to close its lending service. The Curve LP oracle used by Market.xyz was vulnerable to read-only reentrancy in the get_virtual_price() function. Removing liquidity triggered contract fallback logic before pool balances updated, allowing the attacker to inflate the reported LP price and borrow undercollateralized funds.

Adding to the recent string of oracle manipulation attacks is an attack on the miMATIC ($MAI) market on the QuickSwap decentralized exchange. An exploiter was able to manipulate the spot price of assets to borrow funds, ultimately making off with 138 ETH ($188,000) that they mixed through Tornado Cash. The vulnerability was due to the use of a Curve LP oracle, which contains a vulnerability that was disclosed by a security firm earlier that month. Security firm PeckShield initially suggested the issue might have been with QiDAO, which creates the $MAI stablecoin .
